script.text: This jellyfish may never die of old age. It's called Turritopsis dohrnii, and it's smaller than your pinky nail. When it's injured, starving, or under extreme stress, it can transform its adult body back into an earlier stage of its life cycle. It sinks, absorbs its own tentacles, and collapses into a tiny blob. Within a few days, that blob sprouts into polyps — the jellyfish's baby form — which bud off brand-new jellyfish. They're genetic copies of the original. In the lab, they've reset again and again. In the wild, most still get eaten.
